chapter_theme: The close of Sangili Siddhar's kummi: no one is lasting once the soul leaves its cage, so the way is the suzhumunai, yoga without craving, the breath that turns night to day and the single expanse. Holy baths, temple rounds, forest wandering and ritual observance are set against the one test, whether the running mind has stopped and the fourth state, silence, has been reached; and the song ends by telling how Bogar came and named the poet Sangili Siddhar for the chain he wore at his neck.
structure_note: Eleven stanzas. 2134 answers 2133 (no one is lasting); 2135 and 2144 frame the rest with the poet's lineage from Bogar, his பாட்டன்; 2136 to 2138 give the method (suzhumunai, yoga without desire, the night made day); 2139 to 2143 weigh kin, pilgrimage, forest penance, ritual and learning against silence.

2134.reading: Whoever remains, they are not lasting; when our soul leaves the cage and goes, you will see clearly that not one of the townsfolk is lasting, blissful girl.
2134.nuance: கூடு, the cage or nest, is the body the soul leaves; the answer to 2133's string of questions is that no one is சதம், neither the dying nor the townsfolk who outlive him.

2135.reading: Having learned this way, as a siddha both here and in the beyond, know as your own the word of my grandfather, the rishi Bogar, blissful girl.
2135.nuance: பாட்டன், grandfather, is a lineage term; with 2110 (Thirumular as guru) it places the poet in Bogar's line. இகத்தும் பரத்தும், here and beyond, is the siddha's double competence, the claim the medical and alchemical Siddhars make for their art.

2136.reading: Those who wander without knowing the way are crores upon crores in this great land; those who have come to know the suzhumunai have found the way of ease, blissful girl.
2136.nuance: The whole world's wandering is set against one anatomical knowledge; சுகவழி, the way of ease or bliss, picks up the refrain's ஆனந்தம்.

2137.reading: Desire gone, having seen the wisdom of grace, having burnt off and thrown out vain manliness, letting go attachment, do yoga and live in this world, blissful girl.
2137.nuance: வீண் ஆண்மை, vain manliness, may be sexual vigour, to be burnt off as the celibate yogi's discipline, or self-assertion. இந்தப் பாரினில் வாழ்வாய் keeps the yogi in the world, which is the Siddhars' usual stance against the renouncer's departure.

2138.reading: Having turned night into day and known it, having seen and known the one expanse, if you quickly learn this method, this world will praise you, blissful girl.
2138.nuance: இரவைப் பகலாய் இருத்தி is cipher: tradition reads night and day as the moon and sun breaths (left and right channels), so that making night day is bringing the breath to the sun side or the centre; a plainer reading is wakefulness kept through sleep. ஏக வெளி, the single expanse, is the inner space that other Siddhars call the place without night and day.

2139.reading: What if the parents who bore you are alive, what if the wife you took and the children are there? If one does not do good tapas, see, we belong to Yama, blissful girl.
2139.nuance: இருந்தால் என்ன, 'what if they are there', is Pattinathar's formula (277); the stanza adds what the kin cannot prevent, that without tapas one is Yama's kin (நமனுக்கு நாம் சொந்தம்), turning the word for ownership against the family.

2140.reading: Though you bathe at holy waters, though you go round many temples, though you take darshan of the images, say: is the fourth, silence, there, blissful girl?
2140.nuance: நாலாம் மோனம், the fourth that is silence, is read by tradition as the fourth state (துரியம்) beyond waking, dream and sleep; it can also be silence as the fourth path after chariyai, kiriyai and yoga, which fits 2121. On either reading the pilgrimage acts are not condemned, they are asked whether they have produced it.

2141.reading: Though one wanders forests and hills, though one performs ritual observances, for those who have not stopped the running mind the supreme arising does not come, blissful girl.
2141.nuance: கன்மானுட்டானம், the performance of prescribed ritual acts, and forest penance are both measured by one thing, whether the சித்தம் has stopped running. பர உற்பனம் repeats 2119's word for the Supreme's arising in oneself.

2142.reading: Those who have not burnt away the delusion of the world of maya and the infatuation that has fallen on fair women never reach the house of release, blissful girl.
2142.nuance: The two delusions are named together and given one remedy, burning (தீயா, from தீய்த்தல்); the world's maya and a woman's attraction are the same kind of thing for the stanza.

2143.reading: Though one knows the four kinds of arts, though one knows the ways of jnana, only those who know the higher silence reach the release that does not sleep, blissful girl.
2143.nuance: நாலாவகைக் கலைகள் may be the four Vedas, four classes of learning, or the sixty-four arts counted in four; even ஞான வழிகள், the ways of jnana as taught, are placed below மோனம், which 2140 called the fourth. துஞ்சா வீடு, the release that does not sleep, is release that does not lapse or die.

2144.reading: While he wore a chain at his neck and did good tapas and yoga there, my grandfather came and proclaimed him 'Sangili Siddhar': know the word, blissful girl.
2144.nuance: The stanza explains the poet's name, Sangili (chain), and attributes it to Bogar, the பாட்டன் of 2135; it is the song's signature. The third person (அணிந்துகொண்டு ... இருக்கையிலே ... என்று) is the poet speaking of himself.

links.note: The Kural's life leaves the body as a bird leaves its குடம்பை; Sangili's soul leaves the கூடு, the cage or nest, and goes. The same image of the body as a bird's left dwelling, used by the Kural for the thinness of the body-life bond and by Sangili for the unreality of all who remain.

Pattiragiriyar asks when he will stand unobstructed in the sushumna that moves between ida and pingala; Sangili says those who know the suzhumunai have found the way of ease while crores wander. The same channel is the way in both, as a longing in the one and as a finding in the other.

Agasthiyar's guard verse subsides in the unceasing suzhumunai and goes by the vaasi to the summit; Sangili makes knowing the suzhumunai the one way against the world's wandering. Both make the central channel the method itself and not an aid to it.

The Kural says the domain of the five must be crushed and all one wanted let go at once; Sangili says to burn off desire and attachment and then do yoga and live in this world. The letting-go agrees; Sangili's yogi stays in the world where the Kural's chapter is on renunciation.

Tirumular's long-haired lady dances where there is neither night nor day, and one who sleeps there becomes a child age does not touch; Sangili turns night into day and sees the single expanse. In both, night and day are read by tradition as the moon and sun breaths, and their ending is the yogi's state.

Pattinathar says the Lord showed him the place where night and day are no more; Sangili tells the listener to make night day and see the one expanse. The same place, given by grace in the one and reached by method in the other.

Pattinathar asks 'what if there is a town, good people, the mother who bore one, the wife, glory', and Sangili asks 'what if the parents live, what if wife and children are there'; both use இருந்தென்ன and both answer that none of it avails. Sangili names what does avail, tapas, and what otherwise owns us, Yama.

Tirumular ranks temple, bathing and breath below clear knowledge, in whose mind the Lord dwells; Sangili grants the holy bath, the temple rounds and the darshan and asks whether the fourth, silence, has come. Both leave the acts standing and set the test elsewhere.

Pattinathar went as far as Kasi and wore out his legs because he did not watch the breath; Sangili asks whether bathing, temple rounds and darshan have produced silence. In both the pilgrimage is not false but beside the point.

Kakapusundar says forest or town, what matter, once silence is seen, and a lamp carried outside is wasted; Sangili says forests and hills and ritual observance gain nothing for one whose mind still runs. Both make the place of practice indifferent and the stilled mind the whole matter.

The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and all else noisy show; Sangili says forest wandering and ritual acts yield no supreme arising to one whose mind runs. Both locate the test in the mind and treat the visible acts as secondary.

Kanjamalai Siddhar warns that desire for women will not do, that its delusion does not go easily, and that one burns in the fire of desire-bonds; Sangili says those who have not burnt away the world's maya and the infatuation for women never reach release. The same two delusions, and fire on both sides, to be burnt in or to burn away.

Sangili says only those who know the higher silence reach undying release; the Puranamalai lists 'those who say the release called silence' among the people who do not know the Lord's name. On the reading that 751 rejects silence taken as release, the two make opposite claims about mounam; on the reading that it rejects only the saying of it, Sangili's knowers of silence are exempt.

Tirumular's silent ones (மோனர்) whose mind has become full of Siva are the Siva-freed, beyond the powers just listed; Sangili's knowers of the higher silence reach undying release where knowers of the arts and of jnana's ways do not. Both place silence above knowledge and attainment.

source_issues: 2144 line 4: சாற்றைத்தெரியும் is not a regular form; read as சாற்றினதைத் தெரிவாய் or சாற்றைத் தெரி (know the proclamation). The reading is uncertain.
2137 line 2: சுட் டறுத்து த்தள்ளி has a stray space before த்தள்ளி; read சுட்டறுத்துத் தள்ளி.
2141 line 1 is a syllable short against the kummi metre (காடு மலைகள் அலைந்தாலும்); a word may be lost.
The chapter break at 2133/2134 cuts a question from its answer; see ch108.
